findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the MySQL database files, automated backups, and snapshots are stored unencrypted and readable by anyone with access to the underlying storage.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the catalog database a public IP/DNS name reachable from the internet, and the output catalog_db_endpoint advertises it, turning the database into an internet-facing target for brute force and exploitation.

The instance user_data embeds the database password ('${var.password}') in cleartext into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc; instance user data is readable via IMDS and stored in Terraform state, so the admin credential is exposed.

The master username is the well-known 'admin' and the password is a single static variable with ignore_changes on password, so there is no rotation and the account is the classic target for credential attacks.
The ingress rule permits TCP/3306 from the entire VPC CIDR (portal_vpc.cidr_block), not just from the catalog_app_server security group, allowing any host in the VPC to reach the database port.
backup_retention_period = 0 disables automated backups of the database, preventing point-in-time recovery after data loss or a tampering/ransomware event.
monitoring_interval = 0 disables enhanced monitoring, and multi_az = false removes failover, leaving the database without the observability needed to detect credential abuse or intrusion.

The instance role allows s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource '*', so a compromise of the web server (or of anything that can reach IMDS) grants full control of all S3 data, EC2 instances, and databases in the account.

The role's assume-role policy trusts ec2.amazonaws.com with no condition limiting which instances may assume it, and the role is attached to the internet-facing catalog_app_server, amplifying the over-broad catalog_app_policy via IMDS credential theft.
The database security group allows all protocols and all ports (protocol '-1', ports 0) to 0.0.0.0/0, so a compromised DB host can exfiltrate data or reach the internet without restriction.

No database parameter or option group setting enforces SSL/TLS for client connections (e.g. require_secure_transport), so credentials and query data can travel in cleartext to the publicly reachable endpoint.

The database security group is defined with no ingress rules of its own and egress is fully open; combined with the ingress rule living outside the SG, the network posture of the database is defined only by permissive stand-alone rules with no defense in depth.
